description: Central-scenario GG26 ballots by mode per county and statewide (county = Maryland), anchored on the ballots already cast: early = GG26 early-voting total (the board's unofficial eight-day file; early voting is over); mail = GG26 mail received so far x late_multiplier (GG22 certified vote-by-mail / GG22 received the same number of days before election day), capped at GG26 sent and at 0.9 x ballots; provisional at GG22's share of the county's ballots; election day = the rest. return_rate is projected mail / sent. County ballots are the central means rounded by largest remainder to sum to the statewide central total (each within 1 of forecast_county.csv). gg22_share_* are GG22's actual mode shares.

sources.mail: skipjack.db turnout_counts: GG26 family 'sent-returned' county ALL measure sent, every daily as_of; GG22 and PG24 family 'mail-voting' county ALL sent and received at the latest as_of
sources.early: skipjack.db turnout_counts: GG26 family 'early-voting' county-party total and eligible at the latest as_of; GG26 and GG22 family 'sent-returned' county sent and received (GG26 latest, GG22 the same number of days before election day); GG26 family 'same-day' county-party and county, GG22 family 'same-day' county, at the latest as_of

level_rule: Three scenarios per party p, on the logit scale, per draw k:
central: alpha = (1 - w_p) * alpha*_{GG22,p,k} + w_p * alpha*_{GG18,p,k}
w_p starts at 0.5 and moves by 0.1 per index vote, bounded to [0.2, 0.8]. Votes, per party p (DEM, REP, OTH), each in {-1, 0, +1} where +1 means 2018-like and -1 means 2022-like:

1. Registration momentum: position = (m26 - m22) / (m18 - m22) using indices.csv reg_momentum, reg_momentum_2022, reg_momentum_2018 (statewide row for p). Vote +1 if position >= 2/3, -1 if <= 1/3, else 0. If |m18 - m22| < 0.002 the analogues cannot discriminate: vote 0. Amendment: a position outside [-0.5, 1.5] extrapolates beyond the two analogues and its sign is not interpretable: vote 0 when position < -0.5 or > 1.5; otherwise the thresholds above apply.

2. Mail requests, per registrant: project GG26 final sent for p as a linear trend over the available daily snapshots extended to 2026-10-27 (the request deadline; an assumption: no ballots are sent after it). Index = (projected GG26 final sent_p / 2026 projected active_p from denominators_gg26.csv) / (GG22 final sent_p (2022-11-28 file) / GG22 active_p from training.csv), so registration growth is not read as engagement. Vote +1 if >= 1.05, -1 if <= 0.95, else 0. (No 2018 analogue exists: 2018 predates the permanent mail-in list, so this index can only say "more or less engaged than 2022".)

3. Primary participation, per registrant: index = (GP26 ballots_p / GP26 active_p) / (GP22 ballots_p / GP22 active_p), from training.csv (DEM and REP; GP26 split estimated; OTH gets vote 0 because primaries are closed). Vote +1 if >= 1.05, -1 if <= 0.95, else 0. Caveat: GP26 had an incumbent governor and GP22 an open seat, which depresses this index for reasons unrelated to November.

4. Ballots banked before election day, per registrant: banked = early-voting ballots (GG26: the board's unofficial eight-day county-by-party file at its latest as_of; GG22: the certified early-voting count in training.csv) plus mail ballots received back by the same number of days before election day (sent-returned county files; GG22 at the latest daily file on or before its election day minus that many days). Index = (GG26 banked_p / 2026 projected active_p) / (GG22 banked_p / GG22 active_p). Vote +1 if >= 1.05, -1 if <= 0.95, else 0. Caveat: voters have been moving from election day to early voting and mail, so part of a high index is a change of habit rather than more voters; the vote is one step of 0.1, like the others. (No 2018 analogue: 2018 has no daily mail-return files and predates the permanent mail-in list.)
level_rule.csv also records the raw-count ratios (mail_count_ratio, primary_count_ratio, banked_count_ratio) beside the per-registrant indices that vote.
mail_note: No 2018 analogue exists: 2018 predates the permanent mail-in list, so the mail index can only say more or less engaged than 2022. The rule's GG26 projection is an OLS line of sent on calendar day over every daily snapshot, extended to 2026-10-27, the mail-in request deadline (assumed to be when sending stops), floored per county x party at the latest observed count. The mail vote depends on the projection choice: the sent series is step-like, so the all-snapshot slope is much steeper than the last few days', and holding the latest count or extending the last three snapshots gives lower indices (see the _latest and _recent columns of level_rule.csv and the central_mail_latest and central_mail_recent scenarios). No GG22 trajectory of daily sent counts exists to anchor the choice. Once a snapshot dated on or after the deadline is in, every method uses the latest count, since sending is over, and the sensitivities equal the rule.
early_note: Early voting is read from the board's unofficial eight-day files (early-voting, county-party), which the State Board prints while the campaign runs; the certified early-voting count will differ slightly. Mail ballots received back are the sent-returned county files' received measure (envelopes back, before the canvass accepts or rejects them). The 2022 comparison point is the GG22 daily file the same number of days before its election day (November 8, 2022), from the backfilled daily reports. The banked index treats early and mail ballots alike, so a voter who moved from election day to early voting since 2022 raises it without adding a ballot.
sdr_note: Same-day registration adds voters who are not in the September-based 2026 active registration. The reference levels already carry the same-day registrants of their own year, because certified ballots cast include them, so the forecast adds only the excess of 2026's same-day new registrants over GG22's, scaled to 2026 registration: extra_c = sdr26_c - sdr22_c * active26_c / active22_c, where sdr22_c is GG22's new registrants during early voting and on election day (same-day county file) and sdr26_c is GG26's early-voting new registrants (latest same-day county file) plus GG22's election-day new registrants in the county times the statewide growth of early-voting same-day registration from 2022 to 2026. Each county's extra is split by party in proportion to GG26's early-voting same-day new registrants (county-party file; the statewide party mix where a county has none) and added to every scenario as ballots with no noise: every same-day registrant votes. Address changes at the polls are voters already on the rolls and add nothing. GG22 serves as the same-day reference for all scenarios: 2018 allowed same-day registration only during early voting and its same-day files are not in the data. Rates on active keep the September-based denominator.

composition.centring: Every scenario uses comp_centred_cp = comp_cp minus the weighted mean over counties of comp for party p (weights: 2026 projected active registration, denominators_gg26.csv). composition_factors.csv's comp is positive in every cell (statewide DEM +0.051, REP +0.080, OTH +0.034), but its statewide level is not identified: the 2022 mix comes from today's voter file, which lacks the ~13% of the 2022 electorate who have since died or moved, and that bias is as large as the factor. Centred, composition only redistributes turnout across counties within a party and the level comes from the calibrated scenario.
composition.sensitivity: central_comp_level uses the uncentred comp with the central level; its statewide difference from central is the measure ballots_minus_central in forecast_statewide.csv.
composition.structure: The midterm structure effect s_cp is treated as describing the 2022 composition, and comp is a change from it.

eps: Antithetic cell noise: for draws 1-500 eps_cpk is a fresh N(0, sigma_obs^2) per cell, and draws 501-1000 reuse the negated eps of draws 1-500 (eps_{c,p,k+500} = -eps_{c,p,k}); each draw's eps is still marginally N(0, sigma_obs^2) and shared by every scenario within the draw. With 1,000 independent eps the Monte Carlo SE of the statewide OTH mean is about 250 ballots (0.077%), so the 0.1% identity check passed or failed by seed; the antithetic pairs cancel the linear part of that error (identity errors at most about 6e-5 across six seeds tested).
interval_note: Each draw's level is calibrated to a reference year, so the intervals within a scenario carry only the cell noise eps and the shift of the 2026 cells' active registration and comp relative to the reference mix; the spread between low, central and high is the level uncertainty. The range to quote is headline_range: low's q05 to high's q95, around the central mean.
mail_voting_note: GG22 and PG24 mail-voting are read at MAX(as_of) per election, which is the board's 2026-04-21 re-fetch of each certified file (it differs from the original 2022-12-08 and 2024-12-11 files by about 100 ballots sent and a few received).

The 2022 comparison point is the GG22 daily file the same number of days before its election day (November 8, 2022), from the backfilled daily reports.
